items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The great drummers were like that, your Sid Catlett and those people, Jo Jones.

ctx.x: Was that a significant part of what you saw, experienced, absorbed, during the Hampton family band days?

Yes. We played with dancers. We played for dancers, behind dancers. They were always modern. They were always in advance of the normal rhythms that were being played. So I really saw the connection between them when I found out that some of the drummers were dancers. It helped to develop their sense of time. See, that’s the drummer’s main thing. He has to develop a great sense of time. The great drummers were like that, your Sid Catlett and those people, Jo Jones. They weren’t actually always playing the beat,…

When you were in the Hampton family band days, in articles you mentioned the Pettiford family, and I just made a joke the other day about the Marsalis thing – how aware were you of other family bands, and of the tradition of family bands? Or did you just take it for granted, because that’s what your family did?
